final_diagnosis.text: Miliary tuberculosis with repeatedly negative initial microbiological tests, mistaken for sarcoidosis on non-necrotising granulomas, treated with high-dose steroid and complicated by secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis

final_dx.text: Miliary tuberculosis with repeatedly negative initial microbiological tests, mistaken for sarcoidosis on non-necrotising granulomas, treated with high-dose steroid and complicated by secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis

secondary_findings: Secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (fever, cytopenias, ferritin 7821 ug/L, soluble IL-2 receptor 7593 ng/L, CXCL9 52 784 ng/L, marrow haemophagocytes; H-score 256)
Acute hypoxic respiratory failure and shock from day 18 (acute respiratory distress syndrome suspected)
accepted_differential: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis from another trigger (EBV, lymphoma)
red_herrings: Negative sputum AFB smears, MTB PCR and mycobacterial cultures
Negative first cell-free DNA and pathogen sequencing
Non-necrotising (non-caseating) granulomas in the lung and marrow
key_discriminators: Random miliary nodules with four months of fever, cough, night sweats and weight loss
The low sensitivity of every single TB test in miliary disease
No response to high-dose steroid, then worsening
Pancytopenia with rising ferritin and transaminases (secondary haemophagocytosis)
Repeat sequencing and second lavage AFB stain and PCR positive on day 25
teaching_points: In miliary disease a negative IGRA, smear, PCR, culture or even cell-free DNA sequencing does not exclude tuberculosis; pretest probability should drive empirical treatment.
Non-necrotising granulomas do not separate tuberculosis from sarcoidosis; sarcoidosis is a diagnosis of exclusion.
Never start high-dose steroid for presumed sarcoidosis without cover when miliary tuberculosis is still possible.
In secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, treating the trigger is the only intervention clearly linked to survival.
ground_truth.treatment_given: High-dose steroid for presumed sarcoidosis (curator's day 7); then dexamethasone and etoposide (HLH-2004, day 15); empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics and antifungals, intubation and vasopressors from day 18; rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol from day 25 with HLH chemotherapy withheld.
ground_truth.outcome: Multi-organ failure; died about one week after starting anti-tuberculosis treatment. Autopsy declined, so whether tuberculosis was present from the start or reactivated under immunosuppression is not proven; the authors think it was present from the start, and the case follows them.

must_do.text: Keep tuberculosis high on the list despite negative tests, given the miliary pattern, the symptoms and the origin
Start empirical anti-tuberculosis treatment when suspicion stays high despite negative tests, and before or with any steroid
Send samples from more than one site (sputum and lavage, marrow, urine, blood or liver) for AFB stain, MTB PCR and mycobacterial culture, and repeat testing when the course changes
Recognise secondary haemophagocytosis (cytopenias, ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen, soluble IL-2 receptor, marrow) and treat its trigger
Isolate the patient while tuberculosis is possible and involve infectious diseases early
Notify public health and arrange screening of household contacts

must_not_do.text: Diagnose sarcoidosis and start high-dose steroid without anti-tuberculosis cover while miliary tuberculosis has not been reliably excluded
Treat haemophagocytosis with etoposide or escalating immunosuppression without treating the trigger
Take a negative interferon-gamma release assay, smears or sequencing as excluding miliary tuberculosis and commit to sarcoidosis

gaps.item: Complete vital signs on admission (blood pressure, respiratory rate, SpO2)
gaps.guidance: Temperature and heart rate are reported. Blood pressure normal; respiratory rate mildly raised; SpO2 normal or mildly reduced on air at admission.

gaps.item: General and chest examination
gaps.guidance: Thin, unwell, febrile; mild pallor; lungs may be clear or have scattered fine crackles (miliary disease is often quiet on auscultation); no clubbing.

gaps.item: Abdominal examination and lymph nodes
gaps.guidance: Spleen palpable or not (moderate splenomegaly on CT); liver edge possibly palpable; no significant peripheral lymphadenopathy unless Atul decides otherwise.

gaps.item: Fundoscopy (choroidal tubercles)
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Do not invent a near-pathognomonic sign: the Case Reviewer decides; default no abnormality seen.

gaps.item: TB contact history, previous TB treatment, BCG vaccination, date of immigration
gaps.guidance: Not reported. No known contact and no previous treatment; BCG likely given in childhood; the Case Reviewer sets the immigration date.

gaps.item: Occupation, smoking, alcohol, drugs, sexual history, travel
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Neutral answers; no immunosuppressing risk (HIV negative).

gaps.item: Current medicines and allergies
gaps.guidance: None regular before admission; no known allergies.

gaps.item: Rest of the blood count on admission (MCV, lymphocytes, red cell indices) and day 17
gaps.guidance: The article says 'mild normocytic anaemia': MCV normal; lymphopenia likely. Day 17 consistent with Table 1 pancytopenia.

gaps.item: Inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR, procalcitonin)
gaps.guidance: The article says 'elevated inflammatory markers' without values: CRP and ESR raised; procalcitonin normal or mildly raised.

gaps.item: Renal function, electrolytes, bilirubin, ALP, albumin, LDH on admission
gaps.guidance: Renal function normal; sodium mildly low possible; albumin low; LDH raised; bilirubin and ALP normal or mildly raised on admission, rising by day 17.

gaps.item: Triglycerides and fibrinogen (H-score inputs)
gaps.guidance: Not reported although the H-score was 256: by day 17 triglycerides raised and fibrinogen low, consistent with that score; the Case Reviewer sets values. Decided by the curator: triglycerides 1.9 mmol/L on day 0, 3.4 on day 13, 4.1 on day 17; fibrinogen 5.2 g/L on day 0, 3.2 on day 13, 2.1 on day 17 (an H-score of 256 on day 14).

gaps.item: Serum calcium, ACE, urine calcium (sarcoidosis work-up)
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Calcium normal; ACE normal or mildly raised (non-specific in granulomatous infection).

gaps.item: Blood cultures, including mycobacterial blood culture
gaps.guidance: Routine blood cultures negative. Mycobacterial blood culture: the Case Reviewer decides (the article does not report one).

gaps.item: Urine AFB and mycobacterial culture, and other extrapulmonary samples
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Do not auto-generate: the Case Reviewer sets them, since a positive result would end the case early. Decided by the curator: urine AFB smear negative and urine culture no growth to date (judgement calls).

gaps.item: AFB stain, PCR and mycobacterial culture on the bone marrow
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Do not auto-generate: the Case Reviewer decides; marrow culture is often positive in miliary disease but slow. Decided by the curator: marrow AFB stain negative, MTB PCR not detected and culture no growth to date (judgement calls, low bacillary load as in every other early sample).

gaps.item: Liver biopsy
gaps.guidance: Not done in the article. If ordered: granulomas; the Case Reviewer decides AFB stain and culture results. Decided by the curator: non-necrotising granulomas, AFB stain negative (judgement call).

gaps.item: Lumbar puncture and CSF
gaps.guidance: Not done in the article. The Case Reviewer decides; default normal CSF or mild lymphocytosis. Decided by the curator: normal CSF (no meningism, mild headache with fevers only).

gaps.item: Hepatitis B and C serology, EBV and CMV serology or PCR
gaps.guidance: Not reported individually ('viral work-up negative'): negative or past infection; EBV PCR negative.

gaps.item: Coagulation screen and arterial blood gas at day 18
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Coagulopathy with low fibrinogen; hypoxaemic respiratory failure with lactic acidosis in shock.

gaps.item: Bronchoscopy airway findings
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Airways normal or mildly inflamed; no endobronchial lesion.

gaps.item: Dates of the first-round tests, the steroid and the HLH treatment
gaps.guidance: The text gives no dates; Figure 5 (a timeline image) probably does. The Case Reviewer sets the days before path analysis. Decided by the curator from the text (Figure 5 not available): IGRA, sputum and the serum/urine fungal and other screens day 0; first bronchoscopy with lavage and biopsy day 3; first NGS day 3; steroid day 7; sIL-2R and CXCL9 day 13; marrow day 14; HLH-2004 treatment day 15.

gaps.item: Steroid drug and dose; etoposide dose
gaps.guidance: Not reported. High-dose steroid (for example prednisone 1 mg/kg or pulse methylprednisolone); HLH-2004 dexamethasone and etoposide doses.
